sections.heading: the focus lock
sections.body:
Farrice is the creative strategist who finds the gap between a funded performance brand's strongest proof and the claims, answers, and campaign ideas that proof can safely carry.

Arena: funded U.S. supplement and performance brands. Hub skill: turn public evidence, buyer tension, and claim limits into a campaign-ready review.

No claim is made about lost sales, confusion, ad rejection, legal exposure, or conversion lift.

blocks.label: Create permission ask
blocks.text:
Hi [First name] — I was reviewing Create's public product education and found one answer-layer mismatch worth fixing. A support article says 5mg where the product pages use grams.

The more useful finding is how the NSF quality signal sits beside benefit language like ‘sharper focus,’ which needs its own evidence trail. I turned the public-source review into a one-page visual brief and left your internal evidence assumptions blank.

Would it be useful if I sent it over?

sections.heading: what counts and what does not
sections.body:
Views, likes, saves, profile visits, and impressions are attention. A reply from a relevant owner is buyer interest. A call is problem evidence. A paid scope, deposit, or pilot is buyer proof. Collected cash is the strongest commercial proof.

Current state: no message sent · no qualified reply · no call · no sale · $0 collected.
